subject.title: PR1/5 durable core: residual-gap RFC docs

question: Should OpenClaw publish this separate residual durable-core RFC as the architecture anchor for the follow-on implementation stack?
rationale: Current TaskFlow already owns a substantial overlapping durable-job boundary, while the PR intentionally leaves adoption, ownership, and stack order undecided; docs correctness and green CI cannot establish that product direction. ([github.com](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/skills/taskflow/SKILL.md))

options.title: Discuss before publishing
options.body: Keep the architecture proposal in the PR or a dedicated issue until an owner identifies the concrete residual gaps and sponsors this boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the RFC
options.body: Accept these explicitly provisional, unlisted pages as the upstream design anchor and review the dependent implementation stack against them.

options.title: Keep existing owners canonical
options.body: Decline the separate durable-core layer and redirect any concrete missing behavior into TaskFlow, task, session, delivery, or owner-specific changes.

recommendation.title: Discuss before publishing
recommendation.body: Keep the architecture proposal in the PR or a dedicated issue until an owner identifies the concrete residual gaps and sponsors this boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged TaskFlow history is the strongest evidence-backed ownership signal for deciding whether this RFC complements or duplicates the current substrate.
